p.s: Dear Mrs Smith,
Thank you for your letter.
Surely I'll try to help you as good as I can.
First, I tell you the name of the hotel, it's the Palace Hotel.
Fortunately, it is not far from our college.
For getting from the hotel to the conference, you only have to take bus no.7 and get off at St. James College, where the conference will take place.
About the end-of-conference party I can only say that a band will be playing the whole night, and a special guest I still don't know will be expected.
I suggest to wear casual clothes, I think there's no need of school uniforms.
To answer your last question, I would propose you to attend the local zoo, because many baby animals were born in the past few days.
Dear Mrs Smith, I hope the given information is useful for you.
I'm looking forward to seeing you at the conference.
Yours sincerely,

p.s: The telephone
Could you imagine there's no telephone ringing in an office?
Or to live your live without chatting for hours with your best friend?
Could you?
I can't!
The telephone was invented by Alexander Graham Bell in the end of the 19th century.
It was an invention nobody thought how important and how widespread it would be in future.
Nowadays almost every household in the western world owns a telephone, and calling to relatives or friends spread all over the world is no strange thing.
People need the telephone not only for chatting, but also for exchanging information in a very short and direct way with the possibility to answer immediately.
When I was a child, we had no telephone at home, and I always had to go to a phone box in the centre of our village.
Now I have my own flat, and the first piece of furniture I've bought was the telephone.
I'll never take it away from my home.
